analyzed_vuln.description: decode_strip passes derived small widths (width/4 and width/2) into transform1 without validating minimum size. For tiny frame dimensions (e.g., chroma width == 2), transform1 is called with width==1, and then unconditionally writes dst[width-2] and dst[width-1], causing negative indexing (write before buffer start) into s->tmp1/s->tmp2. The crash is observed in transform1, but the root cause is missing dimension/size guards in decode_strip (and caller path that allows too-small widths).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Fuzzer opens VQC decoder with very small coded dimensions, leading to tiny chroma strip width in decode_frame -> decode_strip(..., width/2). vqc_decode_init allocates tmp1/tmp2 as avctx->width/2 elements, but decode_strip invokes transform1 on width/4 and width/2 intermediates even when these are <2. When width/2 becomes 1, transform1 performs tail writes at indices -1 and 0, triggering a heap-buffer-overflow (2-byte write before allocated tmp buffer).
